findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — Making `.small-action` a flex container neutralizes the action button’s `float: right` without a replacement, so long messages can push the control out of its intended right-aligned position.
app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:124 — No cross-browser visual regression coverage exercises the new flex-order mixin, so legacy-prefixed ordering changes can ship undetected.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — Making `.small-action` a flex container neutralizes the action button’s `float: right` without a replacement, so long messages can push the control out of its intended right-aligned position.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.small-action` is being converted to a flex container with `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)`. Looking at the existing CSS for `.small-action-desc` which is a child, the diff removes `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` and replaces it with `padding: 0 1.5%`. The finding correctly identifies that when a parent becomes a flex container, `float` properties on children are ignored. If there was a `float: right` on an action button within `.small-action` (not shown in the diff but implied by the finding), it would indeed be neutralized. However, I cannot verify from the diff alone that there is actually a `float: right` on an action button - the diff only shows changes to `.small-action`, `.topic-avatar`, and `.small-action-desc`. The finding makes a plausible claim about existing CSS not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:124 — No cross-browser visual regression coverage exercises the new flex-order mixin, so legacy-prefixed ordering changes can ship undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `@mixin order($val)` in mixins.scss (lines 127-133) with multiple vendor prefixes for cross-browser compatibility. The finding correctly identifies that this new mixin is used in the codebase (e.g., `@include order(3)` in header.scss, `@include order(2)` in topic.scss) but there's no indication of visual regression test coverage for these flexbox ordering changes. This is a legitimate concern about test coverage for newly added functionality that affects layout across different browsers. However, it's not a bug since the code itself is correct - it's a testing/coverage concern.
